scope.description: Competitive landscape for a horizontal general-listings marketplace (modeled on OLX/Adevinta/eBay, EU-centric). Spans horizontal classifieds leaders, social and local listing substitutes, consumer-to-consumer recommerce apps, category verticals (motors, real estate, jobs), and merchant feed/marketplace-integration platforms that compete for the same supply, demand, trust, and seller-monetization jobs.
inclusion_logic: horizontal classifieds and local listing marketplaces with broad category coverage and local network effects
social and local substitutes where buyers and sellers transact peer-to-peer outside dedicated classifieds apps
consumer-to-consumer recommerce and resale apps that pull second-hand supply and casual sellers
category verticals (motors, real estate, jobs) that fragment high-value listing categories away from horizontal players
merchant feed and marketplace-integration platforms that route professional-seller inventory across marketplaces
operators with meaningful seller monetization, trust and safety investment, and large audience scale
notes: Business stats are included only when they were found on official investor, newsroom, annual report, or official company pages, with the reported period and scope preserved.

Some substitutes and verticals are private companies, owned by a parent group, or do not publish standalone marketplace metrics (for example Facebook Marketplace inside Meta, Craigslist, OfferUp, Vinted, Mercari, Wallapop, Auto Trader UK, Indeed, and merchant-integration vendors). For those, business_stats is intentionally left empty rather than estimated, so cross-player comparability is limited.

Players span pure local classifieds, social/peer substitutes, dedicated recommerce, category verticals, and B2B integration tooling. They are included where the operating model overlaps the horizontal-listings jobs even when the business model differs.
Real-estate vertical stats (Zillow, Rightmove) are reused from official sources already verified within this repository's real-estate-marketplace landscape.

players.name: Facebook Marketplace (Meta)
players.description: Facebook Marketplace is the largest social-graph local listings substitute, embedded inside Meta's apps. Its enormous installed audience and zero-friction listing flow make it the default casual peer-to-peer alternative to dedicated classifieds, particularly for free local pickup and second-hand goods.

players.name: Craigslist
players.description: Craigslist is the long-standing minimalist local classifieds substitute in North America, spanning for-sale, housing, jobs, gigs, and services. Its low-fee, text-first model and entrenched local habit keep it a durable competitor for casual and high-intent local listings despite limited product investment.

players.name: OfferUp
players.description: OfferUp is a mobile-first U.S. local marketplace focused on in-person and shipped second-hand transactions, with built-in messaging, ratings, and community meetup safety features. Following its combination with letgo, it is a leading dedicated local-listings substitute in the U.S.

players.name: Vinted
players.description: Vinted is the leading European consumer-to-consumer fashion resale marketplace, with strong buyer-protection and integrated-shipping mechanics. It is a major recommerce competitor that pulls casual sellers and second-hand fashion supply away from horizontal classifieds.

players.name: Mercari
players.description: Mercari is a leading consumer-to-consumer recommerce marketplace, dominant in Japan with a U.S. operation, focused on easy mobile listing of second-hand goods across many categories. It is a benchmark for C2C resale liquidity and integrated payments and shipping.

players.name: Wallapop
players.description: Wallapop is a leading Spanish-origin local second-hand marketplace combining proximity-based discovery with shipping, spanning fashion, electronics, motors, and home goods. It is a direct C2C recommerce competitor in Southern Europe with strong local-listings overlap.

players.name: Auto Trader Group (UK)
players.description: Auto Trader is the dominant U.K. automotive marketplace vertical, connecting car buyers with dealers and private sellers and monetizing dealer subscriptions, prominence products, and data. It exemplifies how high-value motors listings fragment away from horizontal classifieds into a specialized vertical.

players.name: Zillow Group
players.description: Zillow is the defining U.S. residential property portal benchmark and the strongest example of a real-estate listings vertical, with category-leading traffic and a large monetized lead-generation engine that fragments housing listings away from horizontal players.

business_stats.source_title: Zillow Group Reports Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year 2024 Financial Results
Zillow Group Reports Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year 2024 Financial Results

players.name: Rightmove
players.description: Rightmove is the clearest portal benchmark for agent-led residential search in the U.K., with dominant attention share and strong monetization around partner visibility. It is a leading example of a real-estate vertical fragmenting property listings away from horizontal classifieds.

players.name: Indeed
players.description: Indeed is the leading global jobs marketplace vertical, aggregating job listings at massive scale and monetizing employer sponsorship and hiring tools. As part of Recruit Holdings' HR Technology segment, it is the dominant example of jobs listings fragmenting away from horizontal classifieds.

players.name: Rithum (ChannelAdvisor)
players.description: Rithum (formed from ChannelAdvisor and CommerceHub) is a merchant feed and marketplace-integration platform that routes professional-seller inventory, pricing, and orders across marketplaces and channels. It competes for the professional-seller relationship and the integration layer that horizontal marketplaces also court.
